about: R5, research studio: verification, validation and reproducibility on one small study. Prairie Town is fictional; its plants, costs and battery are illustrative. Demand, wind and solar follow the real hourly shapes of 19 and 20 August and 3 September 2025 on the Southwest Power Pool grid (town_year.json, EIA-930), scaled to the town as in lesson 0. The benchmark day is made up. The day-before plan has many least-cost schedules; a tie rule fixed in advance (keep the most energy in store) picks one. Every number the page states comes from the model in assets/learn/r05-build-validate.js, solved with HiGHS; `ref` holds those results, precomputed, for when the solver cannot load.

study.question: How much would a 50 MW, 200 MWh battery have saved Prairie Town on Wednesday 20 August 2025?
study.dataNote: Demand, wind and solar: the real hourly shapes of 20 August 2025 on the Southwest Power Pool grid (EIA-930), scaled to Prairie Town as in lesson 0. The plants, costs and battery are illustrative.
symbols: the battery's charging and discharging power in hour t, MW
stored energy at the end of hour t, MWh (the [[state-of-charge|state of charge]])
the battery's energy size, 200 MWh, and what it holds at the start of the day, 100 MWh
the gas [[combined-cycle|combined-cycle]] plant's output in hour t and in the hour before, MW (115 MW before the first hour)

bench.label: a made-up day: 220 MW in every hour except 330 MW from 12:00 to 17:00, no wind or solar
bench.intro: Without the battery, the gas plant runs {benchCC} MW in the flat hours; in the five dear hours it runs flat out and the [[peaker|peaker]] adds {benchPeak} MW, at $100/MWh.
steps: **Discharge.** The battery empties its 200 MWh into the five dear hours: 200 MWh × $100/MWh = {benchAvoided} of peaker output avoided.

**Recharge.** Over the day it puts 200 MWh into store (100 before noon, 100 after, so it ends as it began): 200 ÷ 0.85 = {benchCharge} MWh of charging, from the gas plant's {benchRoom} MW of spare room, at $40/MWh: {benchChargeCost}.

rules.name: Balance
rules.words: Plants + battery discharge − battery charge + unserved = demand, every hour (MW).

rules.name: Stored energy
rules.words: Stored now = stored an hour ago + (0.85 × charging power − discharging power) × 1 hour, in MWh. All the round-trip loss is counted on charging.

rules.name: Gas ramp
rules.words: The [[combined-cycle|combined-cycle]] plant changes by at most 40 MW an hour, from 115 MW.

rules.name: End of day
rules.words: The battery ends the day with the 100 MWh it started with.

rules.name: Sizes
rules.words: Each plant within its size and the weather; battery 0–50 MW, 0–200 MWh.

line.after: E = 200          # battery energy, MWh (the sheet says 200,000 kWh)

bugs.right: Right. The battery holds more than its size: the energy limit was typed in kWh into a model that counts MWh.
bugs.wrong: That check passes here. Compare each result with its physical size first.
bugs.fixed: Fixed: **{ok}**, and stored energy never passes 200 MWh.

Net energy to the town, as the balance rows count it
Stored energy at the end of the day

line.after: supply[t] += d[t] - c[t]   # battery: discharge feeds the town

bugs.right: Right. Charging was counted as supply, so the battery fed the town while filling up: energy from nowhere.
bugs.wrong: That check passes here. Follow the battery through one hour: where does its energy go?
bugs.fixed: Fixed: **{ok}**. The battery now charges when the gas plant has room and discharges in the hours the [[peaker|peaker]] would run.

line.before: # (no rule for the end of the day)
line.after: m.add(e[23] == E0)   # end the day with what it started with

bugs.right: Right. The 100 MWh the battery started with cost nothing in the model, and it sold them in the evening.
bugs.wrong: That check passes here. Compare what the battery holds at the start and at the end.
bugs.fixed: Fixed: **{ok}**. The gap, **{lunchGain}**, is the starting 100 MWh at the peaker's $100/MWh.
bugs.alsoText: Also right: the end-of-day rule has no row in the code. Closure catches the same bug from the results alone.

symptoms: Gas plant's biggest change in an hour, in this solution (limit 40)

line.after: for t in T: m.add(-40 <= cc[t] - cc_prev[t] <= 40)   # gas ramp

bugs.right: Right. The formulation has {rampRows} ramp rows; the code has {rampRowsMissing}. Today the headline happens not to move.
bugs.wrong: That check passes here: the saving is the same as the fixed versions. Count each rule's rows in the code.
bugs.fixed: On **{lesson0Label}** the same code says the day without a battery costs **{l0missingBase}** instead of **{l0base}**, and that the battery saves **{l0missing}** instead of **{l0ok}**.

line.after:
plan = solve(day='2025-08-19', tie='keep')  # the last full day measured at 00:00 on 20 August
result = run(day='2025-08-20', battery=plan)

bugs.right: Right. The schedule is set at midnight, as 20 August begins: all 24 hours of 19 August are measured by then, and none of 20 August.
bugs.wrong: That check passes here. Ask what had been measured when the schedule was set, at midnight.
bugs.fixed: Planned on 19 August's measured day (a [[persistence-forecast|persistence forecast]]) and then followed: **{honest}**, {honestShare}% of the {ok} that [[perfect-foresight|perfect foresight]] gives.
bugs.tie: Many schedules tie at {planCost} on 19 August. The rule, set in advance: keep the most energy in store. One that empties the battery first ties too, yet saves only {honestEarly} on 20 August.

benchSaw: The benchmark catches versions 1, 2 and 3. **Version 4 passes**: on this day the ramp limit never binds, so leaving it out changes nothing. A benchmark tests only what it exercises.

why.balance: That is verification: it checks the code against its own equations.
why.bench: That is verification too: the hand answer comes from the same equations.
why.measured: Validation compares what the model predicts with what was measured on the real system.
why.clone: That is reproducibility: the same numbers again, right or wrong.

validationText: The plan's prediction of 20 August is its forecast: 19 August's measured net load (demand minus wind and solar). Compare it with 20 August as measured. Tolerance, set first: the battery's 50 MW, in every hour.
validationSaw: The forecast misses by **{fcMAE} MW** on average and **{fcMax} MW** at {fcMaxHour}: beyond the tolerance in {fcOver} of 24 hours. So the claim is narrowed: **{honest}** with this forecast; **{ok}** only as an upper bound.

inputCheck.text: One input can be checked against measured data: the [[round-trip-efficiency|round trip]]. The study assumed 85% (NLR's 2025 ATB); the U.S. battery fleet averaged 82% in 2019 (EIA). Does the saving hinge on it?
inputCheck.saw: **{eta82}** instead of **{ok}**: {eta82Change}% less, so the conclusion does not hinge on this input. That is an input check and a [[sensitivity-analysis|sensitivity run]], not a validation of the saving.

options: The code reads a data file by a path on one laptop, and the file was never committed
A random seed was not fixed

why.solver: No: the error is a missing file, before any solve.
why.path: Yes: an absolute path and an uncommitted data file. The clean clone has neither.
why.seed: No: this model draws no random numbers.
why.git: No: Git keeps what was committed; this file never was.

fixes: A download script with the source's address, access date and [[checksum|checksum]], so the data can be rebuilt
Paths relative to the repository, never to one laptop
The environment pinned: the exact versions of Python, SciPy and its HiGHS, written in a file such as environment.yml
A tag, a fixed name such as v1.0, on the [[commit|commit]] that made the reported numbers
logAfter: $ git clone <repository> fresh && cd fresh && git checkout v1.0
$ conda env create -f environment.yml    # the pinned versions
$ python get_data.py    # downloads the data, checks its SHA-256

reproSaw: **Simulated:** this page cannot clone anything. With the four fixes, a fresh clone would rebuild the data, print **{ok}** again and match the first run's checksum. Do the real rerun in the notebook's practice; log it once the checksums match.
